headline: Ukraine intelligence: Russia hired Bangladeshi mercenaries for war
summary: Ukrainian intelligence claims to have intercepted communications revealing the presence of Bangladeshi nationals fighting as mercenaries for Russian forces in Kharkiv.
details: Ukrainian intelligence intercepted a phone call between Russian soldiers, in which one soldier mentioned finding two 'foreign mercenaries' from Bangladesh who had lost their way in the Kharkiv battlefield.
caption:
Bangladeshi nationals found fighting for Russia? Ukrainian intelligence claims to have intercepted calls revealing their presence in the Kharkiv war zone.

Ukrainian intelligence intercepted a phone call between Russian soldiers, in which one soldier mentioned finding two 'foreign mercenaries' from Bangladesh who had lost their way in the Kharkiv battlefield.

Source: Prothom Alo

headline: 0-0 at halftime: Colombia and Switzerland tied in high-stakes clash
summary: Colombia dominated possession and attacks in the first half, but failed to convert chances into goals.
details: Colombia and Switzerland are locked in a 0-0 draw after the first 45 minutes of their crucial match to decide who faces Argentina in the quarter-finals.
The Latin American side showed clear dominance on the field, controlling the pace and putting immense pressure on the Swiss defense.
Colombia recorded more shots, earned more corners, and penetrated the opponent's penalty area more frequently than Switzerland.
The Swiss defenders were forced to make 17 clearances in the first half alone to stop the relentless Colombian attacks.
Despite the dominance, Colombia struggled with finishing, a recurring issue for them throughout the tournament.
Switzerland's Manuel Akanji and his teammates fought bravely to keep the clean sheet despite being pinned back for most of the first half.
caption:
Colombia dominated the pitch, but the scoreboard remains empty. 0-0 at the half!

Colombia and Switzerland are locked in a 0-0 draw after the first 45 minutes of their crucial match to decide who faces Argentina in the quarter-finals.

The Latin American side showed clear dominance on the field, controlling the pace and putting immense pressure on the Swiss defense.

Colombia recorded more shots, earned more corners, and penetrated the opponent's penalty area more frequently than Switzerland.

The Swiss defenders were forced to make 17 clearances in the first half alone to stop the relentless Colombian attacks.

Despite the dominance, Colombia struggled with finishing, a recurring issue for them throughout the tournament.

Switzerland's Manuel Akanji and his teammates fought bravely to keep the clean sheet despite being pinned back for most of the first half.

#Colombia #Switzerland #WorldCup #Football #Soccer

Source: Jamuna TV
